title: Linkability of Student Submission Data
description: Student's assignment submission (work file, student id, course, timestamp) could be linked to their identity across systems or time, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of academic behavior.
assumptions: Student data is retained and accessible across multiple systems or time periods.

title: Identification of Student via Submission Data
description: Student id included in assignment submission could be used to identify the student, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized parties if data is intercepted or leaked.
assumptions: Student id is transmitted with the submission and could be accessed by unauthorized actors.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Assignment Data
description: Assignment work file, student id, course, and submission timestamp could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or insecure data transmission.
assumptions: Data is transmitted or stored without adequate access controls and encryption.

title: Usurpation of Student Identity via Login
description: Student login credentials could be compromised, allowing unauthorized actors to submit assignments on behalf of the student or access their academic records.
assumptions: Login credentials are stored or transmitted insecurely, or session management is inadequate.

title: Transmission of Student Identifying Information
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This flow contains unique references to the identity of the data subject (student), creating an identifier threat at the source process.
assumptions: Student id and course information are unique identifiers that can be used to identify the student across systems.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node I.2.1.1 from context as it directly addresses identifier threats in data flows.

title: Processing of Identified Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) receives and processes identified data (student id, course, file reference, requesting role) from the portal. This constitutes processing of identified data, which is a privacy concern when such data is handled without appropriate safeguards.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading and assignment management purposes.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node I.1.1 from context as it addresses processing of identified data.

title: Non-repudiation of Submission and Grading Actions
description: The flow involves submission and grading requests where the requesting role and student id create evidence of involvement. Students or instructors may be unable to deny claims about their involvement in the system due to the data collected (student id, requesting role, file reference).
assumptions: The data transmitted creates audit trails that could be used to attribute actions to specific individuals.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nr.1.1 is inferred from context [4] on non-repudiation threats; exact node may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure via Assignment Storage
description: The Assignment & Grading Service stores assignment files containing student identifiers, course information, and submission timestamps. This creates a risk of implicit data disclosure where personal data (student IDs linked to academic work) could be accessed by unauthorized parties through the data store, or disclosed through metadata patterns.
assumptions: The data store DS1 may have access controls that are not sufficient to prevent unauthorized access, or the data could be accessed through system vulnerabilities or insider threats.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for data disclosure in Process→DataStore flows based on context [4] and [5].

title: Explicit Data Disclosure by Design
description: The system intentionally stores assignment files with student identifiers as part of its core functionality. This represents an explicit disclosure where personal data is transferred to the data store by design, which may violate the minimality principle if the stored data exceeds what is strictly necessary for grading purposes.
assumptions: The data minimality principle requires that only essential personal data be stored. Storing full assignment files with student IDs may exceed this requirement.
uncertainty_note: Context [5] defines Dd as including both explicit and implicit disclosures. This threat captures the intentional storage aspect.

title: Processing of identifiable student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes student submission data that contains personally identifiable information (names, student IDs, etc.) during the teacher review workflow. This processing of identified data creates privacy risks as the system must handle sensitive student information.

title: Unauthorized access through compromised teacher credentials
description: The teacher (ExternalEntity EE3) logs in to access the submission queue. If authentication mechanisms are weak or credentials are compromised, an attacker could impersonate the teacher and gain unauthorized access to student submission data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App displays student submission data to the teacher. If access controls are not properly enforced, student data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties or leaked through the interface.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student personal information
description: Teacher could share student names, work content, or submission times with unauthorized third parties or use the information for purposes beyond educational assessment
assumptions: Teacher has access to the portal and could potentially share data externally

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: Teacher could correlate student submission data with other student information they have access to, creating comprehensive profiles that reveal patterns or sensitive information
assumptions: Teacher has access to multiple student information systems

title: Unauthorized modification of student submission data
description: Teacher could alter displayed student work or submission records before or after viewing, compromising data integrity
assumptions: Teacher has write access or can modify displayed content

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records containing student id, course, grade, and feedback could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, exposing sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Access controls may be insufficient or bypassed

title: Student and Grader Identification
description: Student id and grader id in grade records enable direct identification of individuals, potentially leading to deanonymization when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Student and grader identifiers are unique and traceable

title: Grade Record Tampering
description: Grade records could be altered or corrupted during the write operation, compromising data integrity and potentially affecting student records or academic decisions.
assumptions: Write operations may lack adequate integrity controls

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: Grade records stored in DS2 may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, data breaches, or exposure through inadequate encryption or access controls.
assumptions: Storage security measures may be insufficient

title: Linkability of Student Data
description: Student id in grade records could be linked with other student data sources, enabling profiling or cross-referencing of sensitive information.
assumptions: Other student data sources exist and are accessible

title: Identity Impersonation
description: Stored grader id and student id could be exploited for identity impersonation, allowing unauthorized individuals to appear as legitimate graders or students.
assumptions: Identity verification mechanisms may be weak

title: Linkability of student identity to grades
description: The Grades Portal Web App may link the student's identity to their grades and feedback, potentially enabling correlation of academic performance with other personal data.
assumptions: System maintains student identity information alongside grades

title: Identifiability of student through grades
description: Grades and feedback are personally identifiable information that can identify the student, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Grades are unique to each student and can be used to identify them

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades
description: Grades and feedback may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: System has access controls that may be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Usurpation of student access to grades
description: An unauthorized actor may attempt to access another student's grades by impersonating the student or exploiting authentication weaknesses.
assumptions: Authentication system may have vulnerabilities or social engineering risks

title: Data deception in grades presentation
description: The system may present grades or feedback in a misleading manner, potentially through manipulation of display logic or data presentation.
assumptions: System logic for displaying grades may have bugs or be intentionally manipulated

title: Parent Account Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a parent by compromising their login credentials, gaining unauthorized access to another parent's child grades.
assumptions: Weak authentication or credential theft is possible

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: Child grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the system lacks proper access controls or if data is transmitted insecurely.
assumptions: Inadequate access control or insecure data transmission

title: Parent-Child Identity Linking
description: The system may link parent identity to child grades in ways that could be exploited for profiling or tracking across multiple children.
assumptions: System maintains parent-child relationship data that could be correlated

title: Excessive Grade Data Collection
description: The Grades Portal may collect more grade data than necessary for the parent's legitimate access request, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: System retrieves all grades rather than only requested child's grades

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades and academic data
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits sensitive student information (grades, feedback, submission history) to the parent (EE2). Without proper access controls, authentication, and authorization mechanisms, unauthorized parties could intercept or access this data, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Assumes the system lacks robust access controls or authentication mechanisms for parent access to student data.

title: Parent identity usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate a legitimate parent to access a child's grades, feedback, and submission history through the Grades Portal Web App. This could occur through credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering attacks targeting parent accounts.
assumptions: Assumes parent authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential theft or session hijacking.

title: Regulatory non-compliance in student data sharing
description: The transmission of student grades, feedback, and submission history to parents may violate educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA in the US, GDPR in Europe) if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, and parental rights are not implemented correctly.
assumptions: Assumes the system may not fully comply with applicable educational privacy regulations regarding student data disclosure to parents.

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: The grades, feedback, and submission history data transmitted to parents could potentially be linked with other data sources (e.g., other school systems, online profiles) to create a comprehensive profile of the student, potentially revealing sensitive information beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Assumes data could be correlated across multiple systems or platforms.

title: Administrator actions linked to sensitive parent-child relationship data
description: School Administrator (EE4) can link parent-child relationships to other administrative data, potentially revealing family structure patterns and sensitive personal information about students and parents.
assumptions: Administrator has access to multiple data sources that can be correlated
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific context may vary

title: Administrator identity identifiable through account management activities
description: School Administrator's identity can be identified through their account creation, modification, and disabling activities, potentially revealing their role, access patterns, and administrative responsibilities.
assumptions: System logs administrator actions with identity information
uncertainty_note: Likelihood high as logging is standard practice

title: Unauthorized disclosure of parent-child relationship data
description: Administrator may inadvertently or maliciously disclose sensitive parent-child relationship information to unauthorized parties through the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Administrator has access controls that could be bypassed or misused
uncertainty_note: Severity high due to sensitive nature of family relationship data

title: Excessive data collection in account and relationship management
description: Administrator may collect and store more parent-child relationship data than necessary for legitimate administrative purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: System allows collection of all relationship attributes without strict necessity checks
uncertainty_note: Depends on system design and data retention policies

title: Administrator account usurpation or impersonation
description: Administrator account could be compromised or impersonated, allowing unauthorized account creation, modification, or disabling of parent-child relationships.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to compromise
uncertainty_note: Severity high due to potential for significant data manipulation

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations in account management
description: Administrator's account and relationship management activities may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding data handling and consent.
assumptions: System lacks adequate compliance controls or audit mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific regulatory requirements and system implementation

title: Identification of students and family relationships through account records
description: The grading service writes account records containing parent-child relationship links to the account directory. This could allow identification of students and their family connections, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about family structures.
assumptions: Account records contain identifiable information about students and their family relationships

title: Unauthorized disclosure of account records during write operation
description: When the grading service writes account records to the account directory, there is a risk that sensitive student and family relationship data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or logging mechanisms.
assumptions: The account directory may have insufficient access controls during write operations

title: Unauthorized modification of account records and relationship links
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the account directory, creating opportunities for unauthorized modification of these sensitive relationship data, which could lead to false or manipulated family connection records.
assumptions: Write operations to the account directory may not have adequate integrity controls

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary.
assumptions: Third-party provider has access to full personal data including grades and account information
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 chosen based on explicit disclosure pattern; context [5] confirms Dd applies to transfers to third parties

title: Linkability of Personal Data Across Systems
description: Grade records and account directory data transferred to EE5 could be linked with other data sources to create comprehensive profiles of students/users.
assumptions: Third-party may correlate this data with other datasets
uncertainty_note: Linkability threat depends on third-party data practices; assumed based on nature of account directory data

title: Identifiability of Individuals in Transferred Data
description: Account directory and grade records contain direct identifiers (names, IDs, contact info) that make individuals directly identifiable to EE5.
assumptions: Account directory includes personally identifiable information
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 selected for direct identifiability; context [3] confirms I applicable at S/fl/D positions

title: Data Integrity During Transfer to Cloud
description: Nightly backup and replication of sensitive grade and assignment data to external provider creates risk of data tampering or corruption during transmission.
assumptions: Data in transit or at rest on EE5 could be modified
uncertainty_note: Integrity threat standard for any external data transfer; severity depends on encryption and validation mechanisms

title: Unauthorized Use of Disclosed Personal Data
description: Third-party cloud provider EE5 may misuse or repurpose the transferred personal data (grades, assignments, account info) beyond intended backup purposes.
assumptions: EE5 has capability to access and use data beyond contractual obligations
uncertainty_note: Usurpation threat based on third-party data access; depends on contractual safeguards and provider trustworthiness

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk for Third-Party Data Transfer
description: Transferring personal data to external cloud provider may violate data protection regulations (GDPR, FERPA, etc.) if proper safeguards and legal basis are not established.
assumptions: Data transfer may not comply with applicable privacy laws
uncertainty_note: Compliance threat depends on jurisdiction and contractual arrangements; Nc.1.1 selected for regulatory context

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive student performance data that could lead to privacy violations and potential discrimination.
assumptions: Access controls on DS2 are not properly enforced or are bypassed

title: Student Identification from Grade Data
description: Grade records can be used to identify specific students, potentially exposing their academic performance to unauthorized observers.
assumptions: Grade records contain or can be linked to student identifiers

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Other Data
description: Grade records accessed by the grading service may be linked with other student data (e.g., demographic, behavioral) to create comprehensive profiles.
assumptions: Other data sources exist that can be correlated with grade records

title: Compliance with FERPA/Privacy Regulations
description: The grading service may not comply with educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA) when handling student grade records, leading to legal and reputational risks.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements exist for grade data handling
